Which of the two versions is meant will be clear from context. If there is
any confusion we will distinguish between these by saying that the first
version means <MATH_0001> is essentially constant as an <TEXTITOPEN_0001>ind-object<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>, and in
the second case we will say it is essentially constant as a <TEXTITOPEN_0002>pro-object<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>.
This terminology is further explained in
Remarks <REF_0001> and <REF_0002>.
In fact we will often use the terminology ``essentially constant system''
which formally speaking is only defined for systems over directed sets.

Let <MATH_0001> be a category. A directed system
<MATH_0002> is an <TEXTITOPEN_0001>essentially constant system<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
if <MATH_0003> viewed as a functor <MATH_0004>
defines an essentially constant diagram. A directed inverse system
<MATH_0005> is an <TEXTITOPEN_0002>essentially constant inverse system<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> if
<MATH_0006> viewed as a functor <MATH_0007> defines an
essentially constant inverse diagram.
